issue_context.title: JS - actions are not executed in a form
issue_context.body:
Attach (recommended) or Link to PDF file here:
Original pdf:
https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/866023/IHT205_2004-2006.pdf

A copy: [IHT205_2004-2006.pdf](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/6191219/IHT205_2004-2006.pdf)

Configuration:
- Web browser and its version: firefox nightly
- Operating system and its version: linux
- PDF.js version: 
- Is a browser extension:

Steps to reproduce the problem:
1. Put some numbers into fields for item 11 at page 2

What is the expected behavior? (add screenshot)
Field `A` under `11.11` should contain the sum of numbers entered in field `11.*`

What went wrong? (add screenshot)
Nothing in field `A`.
comments:
The problem is that CO (Calculation Order) contains some references to fields which contain themselves some annotations (annotations and fields are not merged). 
There are some fields which are just containers for other fields, their type is an empty string and there is nothing in spec about that:
https://www.adobe.com/content/dam/acom/en/devnet/acrobat/pdfs/AcrobatDC_js_api_reference.pdf#page=442
Additionally, annotations can inherit their actions from the parent fields.
For these reasons a lot of actions are not executed at all.

review_comments:
*Connected to the comments above:* By always running this method, for every Annotation rather than just WidgetAnnotations, won't this warning now be printed *a lot* for cases where it shouldn't?
Obviously we could remove it and/or change it to `info` instead, but I do wonder about these changes generally.

I'm assuming that there's a particular reason for iterating through this array in *reverse* order, so small comment mentioning why would probably not hurt here (to avoid someone changing that later thinking it won't matter).

*Most a pre-existing issue, but:* You probably want to also wrap the loop below in a `if (additionalActions instanceof Dict) { ... }`-check to avoid throwing if the data isn't a Dictionary (e.g. if the PDF is somehow corrupt).
